Key Lab of HCST (PKU), MOE; School of Computer Science, Peking University; Beijing Tongming Lake Information Technology Application Innovation Center (TLAIC); Fudan University Institute of Systems for Advanced Computing; Shanghai Institute of Systems for Open Computing (academic)

Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — BACKENDFORGE benchmark of 56 contract-defined backend generation tasks rewritten from open-source applications, with an HTTP oracle hardened by multi-agent co-evolution (test, review and code agents); 14 LLM configurations compared under one agentic harness, plus a self-verification variant

No SDD approach evaluated. Harness: a mini-SWE-style agentic coding harness following SWE-agent design (name and version not stated). Models (thinking effort): GPT-5.5 (xhigh), Claude Opus 4.7 (max), Gemini 3.5 Flash, Claude Sonnet 4.6 (max), Qwen 3.6 Max (high), Qwen 3.6 Plus (high), DeepSeek V4 Pro (max and high), GLM 5.1, Kimi K2.6, DeepSeek V4 Flash (high and max), Hunyuan Hy3 (high), MiniMax M2.7. Variant: hidden self-verification tool (backendforge_self_verify)

Benchmark input is a visible task contract: spec.md (roles, ownership rules, state transitions, workflow side effects, mock-service contracts) and openapi.yaml (endpoints, request/response schemas, status codes, authentication). Required output: a Python backend service and a Dockerfile; framework, storage and internal design are free

Agent run: read files, edit code, run tests, inspect failures, revise code, submit; evaluator builds and deploys the Docker service and runs the hidden HTTP oracle. Benchmark construction: (1) task selection and rewriting; (2) base oracle (test agent + review agent) then reference implementation (code agent); (3) multi-agent oracle co-evolution (propose test, run on old reference, review, repair reference, full regression)

Automatic: evaluator builds and deploys the submitted Docker service and runs the hidden pytest oracle over HTTP; costs and tokens from runs. Oracle constructed by LLM test, review and code agents (model not stated) with deterministic regression; categories from recorded bug-pattern metadata

Tasks: 56 tasks with visible spec.md and openapi.yaml. Configurations: 14 model/thinking-effort settings under the same mini-SWE-style harness; variant with hidden self-verification (pass/fail plus coarse phase only) for DeepSeek V4 Pro. Baseline: none designated. Held constant: harness, tasks, oracle, Python-only implementation. Acceptance tests: hidden black-box HTTP pytest oracle, success only if all items pass. Repetitions: not stated (single run per configuration apparently). Human intervention: none

Final oracle: GPT-5.5 best (16/56, 28.6%), Claude Opus 4.7 10/56 (17.9%), every other configuration ≤3/56. Base oracle: Opus 4.7 highest (58.9%), GPT-5.5 55.4%. Adding 640 co-evolved items (+8.8% items) lowers SR by 48% to 100% relative. Top proprietary models cost more ($3.39 GPT-5.5, $5.55 Opus 4.7) than several open-source configurations (sub-dollar). Validation is the largest failed category (23 failed outcomes for GPT-5.5 to 91 for DeepSeek V4 Pro); DeepSeek V4 Pro also 79 authorization and 74 state failures. Hidden self-verification raises DeepSeek V4 Pro from 2 to 7 of 56 tasks; 49 still fail. No significance tests

The co-evolved oracle separated models more sharply than the base oracle (monotonic attrition). Repeatability not assessed (no repetitions reported). The review agent filtered 113 candidate items (overinterpretation, unsupported assertions, contract gaps). Limitations stated: Python backend only; no full-stack UI, other stacks, performance, deployment security or production hardening; oracle bounded by visible contracts and cannot cover all behaviours

Limitations: scope limited to Python backend services and deterministic black-box HTTP tests; no full-stack UI, other stacks, performance, deployment security or production hardening; oracle not exhaustive, so passing does not mean production-ready; dual-use risks. Gap: current LLMs implement many local API behaviours but struggle with validation, authorization, state consistency, side effects and workflows; self-verification helps only partly

Inconsistencies: abstract calls GPT-5.5 'the best-performing model' with 55.4% base SR, but Claude Opus 4.7 has the higher base SR (58.9%); GPT-5.5 is best only on the final oracle. Figure 5 values for GPT-5.5 in the extracted text sum to 78 against a total of 84 (one category value missing). Which DeepSeek V4 Pro setting was used for self-verification is not stated (2/56 matches the max setting). Models used by the construction agents not stated; number of runs per configuration not stated. Artefacts: authors 'intend to release' the benchmark; no repository link given. No pre-registration. Programming language: Python (required for generated services), Docker
